newsitem.title: ITALY: Sale of Olivetti PC business reported imminent.
newsitem.headline: Sale of Olivetti PC business reported imminent.

text.p: The sale of Italian information technology group Olivetti's struggling PC business to a consortium of investors led by an Italian and an American is imminent, Turin newspaper La Stampa reported on Sunday.
The newspaper quoted sources close to Gianmario Rossignolo, the chairman of Electrolux subsidiary Zanussi, as saying that it was hoped that a deal could be finalised by Monday.
Rossignolo has joined forces with U.S. businessman Edward Gottesman, who heads a London-based venture capital company called Centenary Group.

Other investors in the consortium, which is reported to have agreed to pay 200 billion lire ($132 million) for the PC unit, include Italian investment bank Arca merchant and Sofipa, a unit of another Italian bank, Mediocredito, the newspaper reported.
La Stampa reported that the investors were thinking of creating a holding company for the business to be called Piedmont International.
Among those invited to join the board of the PC company if the sale goes through was Elserino Piol, former deputy chairman of Olivetti, who resigned this past July.
Piol was one of the chief business strategists at Olivetti before his departure and is credited with masterminding the group's move into telecommunications.

Olivetti, which has not turned a profit since the 1980s, has pinned its hopes of recovery on its Omnitel Pronto Italia (OPI) mobile telephone venture which has quickly built up a large subscriber base since its launch in early 1996.

Olivetti stepped up its efforts to find a purchaser for its personal computer business after Roberto Colaninno took over the chairmanship of the group late last year, bringing to an end several months of chaos in which Olivetti's share price plunged.
Colaninno said he intended to raise 800 billion lire through asset disposals which he hopes to complete by early 1997.

International investment funds, which hold a large proportion of Olivetti's stock, have urged the company for months to sever its links with the PC business which has been severely squeezed by competition from low-cost producers in the United States and Asia. $=1,530
